security_spec.violation_condition: The spec now removes the sentence 'Modifications to locked spmpcfg[i] and spmpaddr[i] registers are only permitted through execution environment access via miselect.' If XiangShan RTL still implements a write path via miselect (or any other M-mode CSR access mechanism) that bypasses the L-bit lock on SPMP entries, the hardware allows modification of locked entries that should be immutable—violating the revised specification that no longer carves out a miselect bypass.
security_spec.summary: Removal of the miselect bypass for locked SPMP entries means M-mode must not be able to silently unlock/modify S-mode-locked SPMP rules; any remaining miselect write path to locked spmpcfg/spmpaddr in RTL constitutes a hardware privilege escape

findings.finding: All mireg2-6 are ZeroFieldBundle stubs: regOut := 0.U, writes silently dropped. The Smpmpind indirect data registers through which miselect->spmpcfg/spmpaddr writes would be routed are entirely non-functional. No miselect bypass of SPMP L-bit exists because SPMP is not implemented.

All sireg2-6 are ZeroFieldBundle stubs. The Sscsrind indirect data path (siselect->spmpcfg/spmpaddr in S-mode) is non-existent. No S-mode indirect SPMP access path exists, so no L-bit bypass is possible.

Iselect classification: isInAIA(0x30-0x3F), isInImsic(0x70-0xFF), isInOthers(everything else). Any Smpmpind miselect value (e.g., 0x02-0x41) falls into isInOthers, triggering isIllegal. No Smpmpind category exists.

miselect legal ranges: 0x30-0x3F (AIA, even only) and 0x70-0xFF (IMSIC). Values 0x00-0x2F and 0x40-0x6F are illegal. Any Smpmpind miselect value (0x02-0x41 for 64 entries) falls in illegal range. No miselect->SPMP entry selection is possible.

spec_citations.excerpt: The value of miselect determines which register is accessed upon read or write of each of the machine indirect alias CSRs (mireg*). miselect is a WARL register.

findings.finding: MISelectField WARL constraint: maxValue=0xFF, reserved subranges 0x00-0x2F and 0x40-0x6F. These WARL constraints prevent any Smpmpind miselect value from being accepted; any such write would be coerced by WARL to a legal AIA/IMSIC range value.

object MISelectField extends ISelectField(
  maxValue = 0xFF,
  reserved = Seq(
    Range.inclusive(0x00, 0x2F),
    Range.inclusive(0x40, 0x6F),
  ),
)

findings.finding: All mireg2-6 CSR accesses unconditionally flagged illegal. The Smpmpind indirect CSR access channel is actively blocked at the permit stage.

spec_citations.excerpt: The behavior upon accessing mireg* from M-mode, while miselect holds a value that is not implemented, is UNSPECIFIED. It is expected that implementations will typically raise an illegal-instruction exception for such accesses.

findings.finding: MMWP is hardwired Read-Only (RO) with reset=0. Even if SPMP checker hardware existed, SPMP cannot be activated because MMWP is not writable. No L-bit bypass can occur because the SPMP mechanism is architecturally disabled.
findings.snippet: val MMWP  = RO( 1).withDescription("Machine-mode whitelist policy control from the Smepmp extension.")

spec_citations.excerpt: this extension introduces the RLB, MMWP, and MML fields in the mseccfg CSR and their associated rules.

findings.finding: PMPCfgBundle is 8-bit M-mode PMP config layout: R(0), W(1), X(2), A(4:3), ATOMIC(5), C(6), L(7). No SPMP-specific config bundle exists (no SHARED, U, RWX, E fields). Without an SPMP config bundle, there is no SPMP L-bit to bypass.
findings.snippet:
class PMPCfgBundle extends CSRBundle {
  override val len = 8
  val R      = WARL(0, wNoFilter)
  val W      = WARL(1, wNoFilter)
  val X      = WARL(2, wNoFilter)
  val L      = PMPCfgLField(7, wNoFilter)

findings.finding: M-mode PMP L-bit lock logic: 'when (!cfgOldTmp.L.asBool) { cfgVec(j) := cfgNewTmp }'. Locked pmpcfg entries correctly protected on direct CSR address writes. There is no equivalent SPMP L-bit logic to audit because SPMP does not exist.

spec_citations.excerpt: Locked rules cannot be removed or modified until a PMP reset, unless mseccfg.RLB is set.

findings.finding: M-mode PMP address lock logic: checks addrNextLocked/addrLocked. Correctly prevents modification of locked PMP address entries on direct CSR writes. No equivalent SPMP address lock logic exists because SPMP is not implemented.

findings.finding: Only M-mode pmpcfg/pmpaddr CSR addresses (0x3A0-0x3EF) are defined. No spmpcfg (0x1CC-0x1CF) or spmpaddr CSR addresses exist in the decoder, so they cannot be accessed via CSR instructions.
